# Configuration

brig reads its settings from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/brig/config.yaml`, usually `~/.config/brig/config.yaml`. [config.example.yaml](../../config.example.yaml) in the source tree sets every key.

A missing file yields the built-in configuration. Unknown keys are errors.

Non-zero defaults in the file replace built-in ones; a network profile in the file replaces a built-in profile of the same name as a whole.

All keys are optional. A key that you leave out keeps its built-in default, shown below.

## Value types

- **size**: A size such as "512MiB", "8G" or "20 GiB". Units are binary (powers of 1024) whether or not they carry the "i"; a bare number is bytes.
- **duration**: A length of time as config.yaml writes it: a number of days (90d) or weeks (12w), or what time.ParseDuration takes (36h).
- **list of port numbers**: TCP ports from 1 to 65535, written as a YAML list such as `[11434, 8080]`.

## defaults

Defaults are used for settings a command does not set explicitly.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="defaults.cpus"></a>`defaults.cpus` | integer | `4` | The number of virtual CPUs of a new VM. At least 1. |
| <a id="defaults.memory"></a>`defaults.memory` | size | `8GiB` | The memory of a new VM, a whole number of MiB. At least 512MiB. |
| <a id="defaults.root_disk"></a>`defaults.root_disk` | size | `20GiB` | The size of a new VM's root disk, the throwaway overlay of its base image. At least 8GiB. |
| <a id="defaults.data_disk"></a>`defaults.data_disk` | size | `40GiB` | The size of a new VM's data disk, which holds the gateway's state, secrets, images and the sandboxes' workspaces. At least 1GiB. |
| <a id="defaults.network_profile"></a>`defaults.network_profile` | string | `default` | Names the network profile of a new VM. |
| <a id="defaults.fedora_release"></a>`defaults.fedora_release` | integer | `44` | The Fedora release of the base images that brig builds, as its number. |

## network_profiles

A network profile restricts the network destinations a VM can reach. All destinations are denied unless allowed. brig enforces profiles outside the VM, so nothing in the VM can lift them.

[Network profiles](network-profiles.md) lists the built-in profiles and what the keys mean in practice. `NAME` is the name of a profile.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="network_profiles.NAME.internet"></a>`network_profiles.NAME.internet` | boolean | `false` | Allows destinations outside the host, LAN and special-purpose address ranges. |
| <a id="network_profiles.NAME.host"></a>`network_profiles.NAME.host` | boolean | `false` | Allows all services on the host's loopback interface. Without it, the host's own addresses are blocked too. |
| <a id="network_profiles.NAME.host_ports"></a>`network_profiles.NAME.host_ports` | list of port numbers | `[]` | Allows these TCP ports (1 to 65535) on the host's loopback interface even when host is false, e.g. a local model server. |
| <a id="network_profiles.NAME.lan"></a>`network_profiles.NAME.lan` | boolean | `false` | Allows private, shared, link-local and multicast address ranges, and the networks of the host's own addresses and routes, in any routing table, other than default ones, such as a VPN's intranet, when the VM starts. |
| <a id="network_profiles.NAME.ipv6"></a>`network_profiles.NAME.ipv6` | boolean | `false` | Allows IPv6 traffic; otherwise the VM gets no IPv6 connectivity. |

## openshell

OpenShell configures how brig applies OpenShell config directories to the VMs' gateways.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="openshell.secret_tool"></a>`openshell.secret_tool` | string | `secret-tool` | The program brig runs as `SECRET_TOOL lookup ATTRIBUTE VALUE...` to read provider secrets: a name to look up in PATH or an absolute path. Config directories cannot set it, so that one shared with others cannot run programs on the user's host. |
| <a id="openshell.configs"></a>`openshell.configs` | list of strings | `[]` | The config directories of new VMs: absolute paths, where a leading ~/ stands for your home directory. |

## audit

Audit configures the audit trail that brig keeps of each VM.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="audit.journal"></a>`audit.journal` | string | `changes` | Says what the collector mirrors to the user journal: changes (denials, policy and draft changes, sandboxes and gaps), all (allowed requests too) or off. |
| <a id="audit.retention"></a>`audit.retention` | duration | `0` | Deletes the days of history older than it, at least a day; zero keeps everything. |
